claim_text: Pakistan's previous auto policy (AIDEP 2021-26) expired on June 30 2026
notes: Consistent factual/dated event across independent outlets.

claim_text: Draft Auto Policy 2026-31 targets reducing the weighted-average vehicle import tariff from 10.6% to 7.4% by 2030, with a broader net weighted-average target closer to 6% by decade's end
notes: [VERIFY] Draft-stage figure, not a finalized/gazetted policy. Subject to change per ongoing Industries-Commerce dispute (see C-12).

claim_text: Draft tariff structure simplifies duty into four slabs (0%, 5%, 10%, 15%), with CBU imports capped at 15% by 2031
notes: [VERIFY] Draft-stage; the 15% cap is disputed by PAAPAM (see C-06).

claim_text: Draft localization targets: 85% domestic value addition for two-wheelers/light vehicles by 2030; 80-90% local content for small cars by 2031
notes: [VERIFY] Draft-stage, unconfirmed against final policy text.

claim_text: New-energy-vehicle-specific parts would receive a 1% customs duty for the first three years (2026-2029), rising to 5% in year four
notes: [VERIFY] Draft-stage. Note: this specific provision implies roughly a 4-year protection window for NEV parts, not the 5 years assumed in the original angle framing - reconcile before scripting.

claim_text: PAAPAM has demanded customs duties of 50-60% on CBU imports and a minimum of 45% protection on localized components
notes: Direct quoted/reported industry-association position; the position itself (not its merits) is confirmed.

claim_text: PAAPAM states Pakistan's auto-parts industry carries a 34% cost disadvantage against regional rivals, due to 100% import-dependence on raw materials (auto-grade steel, plastic resin, rubber) plus high energy tariffs, taxes, and borrowing costs
source_institution: PAAPAM, via Business Recorder / trade press
notes: This is PAAPAM's own advocacy claim, not an independently audited cost study. Treat as REPORTED/attributed, not a neutral fact - script must attribute it explicitly to PAAPAM.

claim_text: PAAPAM states the auto/parts ecosystem supports over 1 million livelihoods: 300,000+ workers directly employed in manufacturing plus 700,000 in allied services
source_institution: PAAPAM, via Profit by Pakistan Today
notes: [VERIFY] PAAPAM's own estimate; no independent labour-survey figure found to cross-check.

claim_text: The government shelved/withdrew the draft Auto Policy 2026-31 around August 3 2026 after objections it favoured pure EVs so heavily it risked turning Pakistan into an assembly point for imported EV kits
notes: Two independent secondary sources corroborate the same event, raising confidence, but no official government statement or document was directly accessed - [VERIFY] against an official MoIP notice if one exists.

claim_text: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif tasked a committee led by Deputy PM/Finance Minister Ishaq Dar with producing a revised, more balanced auto policy
notes: [VERIFY] against an official notification of the committee's formation.

claim_text: On August 13 2026, the Ishaq Dar-led committee gave 'in-principle approval' to a new draft, which still requires Ministry of Industries incorporation before submission to the federal cabinet
notes: As of the research date the policy had NOT been finalized or gazetted - still in committee-to-cabinet pipeline.

claim_text: As of early-to-mid August 2026, tariff levels remain the single biggest unresolved dispute between the Ministry of Industries (considering a 74% tariff cut paired with an 82% federal excise duty to preserve effective protection) and the Ministry of Commerce (holding firm on the National Tariff Policy's 15% cap by 2030)
notes: [VERIFY] against a primary inter-ministerial document if one becomes available.

claim_text: The IMF rejected Pakistan's proposed 1% sales-tax carve-out for NEVs in the draft policy, insisting on the standard 18% GST rate instead
notes: [VERIFY] Secondary reporting on the IMF's position; the actual IMF correspondence/staff report was not directly accessed.

claim_text: Following the June 30 2026 policy expiry, hybrid vehicles (HEVs/PHEVs) automatically reverted from preferential GST rates (8.5% up to 1800cc, 12.75% above) to the standard 25% GST rate effective July 1 2026 under the FY27 budget
source_institution: Dawn Business / ProPakistani / Profit by Pakistan Today (consistent across multiple outlets)
notes: Consistent, specific, dated tax-rate figures across multiple independent outlets.

claim_text: Indus Motor Company (Toyota) raised prices of its Corolla Cross HEV models by Rs 1.364 million and Rs 1.314 million, to Rs 10.299 million and Rs 9.849 million respectively; Honda Atlas raised its HR-V hybrid price by Rs 1.370 million to Rs 10.369 million
source_institution: Multiple trade press (Bloom Pakistan / Samaa / ProPakistani)
notes: Specific, dated manufacturer price-list changes reported consistently across independent outlets.

claim_text: Some local assemblers temporarily halted invoicing and delivery of hybrid vehicles after the GST change, anticipating a possible policy reversal or GST reduction under the forthcoming auto policy

Under the 2016-21 Auto Development Policy, the number of assemblers grew from a 3-player market to roughly 13-15 manufacturers, but most of over 12 announced Greenfield/Brownfield investment collaborations were pulled off or put on hold, citing currency depreciation and policy volatility
notes: [VERIFY] Not an official/primary tally; cross-check current operating manufacturer count against PAMA membership data before using in script.

claim_text: Under AIDEP 2021-26, motorcycle and tractor exports reportedly reached about 150% of manufacturing-linked targets, while car exports remained under 1% of total production, missing the policy's car-segment export targets
notes: [VERIFY] Primary EDB/PAMA export data not directly accessed; figure is a useful directional finding, not confirmed to primary-source precision.

claim_text: AIDEP 2021-26's consumer-protection provisions (addressing delayed vehicle deliveries) resulted in Rs 5.3 billion being recovered from manufacturers
source_institution: Trade press summary of AIDEP 2021-26 outcomes
notes: [VERIFY] Primary consumer-protection agency data not directly accessed.

claim_text: Pakistan's passenger-vehicle market is roughly 1/25th the size of India's; Pakistani buyers generally pay significantly more for comparable vehicles, especially SUVs and premium segments, due to smaller-scale, less-localized manufacturing and reliance on imported kits
notes: [VERIFY] No single official cross-country price-index figure found; treat as a qualitative/comparative finding, not a precise percentage claim, unless a cleaner figure is found in follow-up research.

claim_text: Pakistan separately introduced an Electric Vehicle Policy 2025-30 (distinct from the Auto Policy 2026-31), offering over Rs 100 billion in subsidies over five years for e-bikes/rickshaws; this EV policy was also reported 'on hold' pending a fresh draft as of August 2026

A locally manufactured EV under the 'Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification (PAVE)' program was targeted for a sub-Rs 1 million price point with a possible mid-2026 (summer) launch, per the EDB chief
notes: [VERIFY] Original target window (summer 2026) appears to have passed with no confirmed launch found in later reporting - status as of the research date is unresolved.

claim_text: The 2016-21 Automotive Development Policy did not set a quantified local-content percentage target - it worked through a duty differential instead: Category-A investors paid 10% customs duty on non-localized parts vs. 25% on localized parts, for a period of five years
source_institution: Board of Investment (BOI), Government of Pakistan
notes: Directly read the primary official document (not a snippet). This is an important framing point: the 2026-31 draft's explicit 80-90%/85% percentage targets (C-04) would be a structural departure from how the 2016-21 policy approached localization - worth making explicit in the script's history section rather than assuming continuity.
